summary: Feed s152_double is degraded: IDS port (1 Gbps) is overloaded by 1.46 Gbps bursts (146% capacity) causing 8.5% TCP packet drops. Both faults correlate and will cause missed IDS detections.

findings.root_cause: 8.5% of TCP packets (155/1828) show gaps/retransmissions indicating packet broker egress buffer drops. Correlated with 1.46 Gbps bursts exceeding the 1 Gbps IDS port, the broker is discarding packets before delivery.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams and misses payload for signature matching, leading to false negatives and evadable attacks. Needs full payload but receives incomplete flows.

recommended_fix.why: Spreading bursts across multiple IDS ports keeps per-port rate below 80% threshold, eliminating buffer overflow drops and restoring complete TCP delivery for detection.

findings.root_cause: Peak traffic hits 1.46 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (146% overload, 5 intervals). Single 1G tool port is undersized for aggregated burst rate from packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC and broker egress queue overflow, causing tail drops, incomplete flow tables, and degraded detection coverage. IDS needs both directions and full payload but is missing data under load.

recommended_fix.why: Hash-based load balancing across 2+ IDS members distributes bursts and keeps each 1G port below 80% utilization, preventing overload drops while preserving flow symmetry for IDS.
